newsitem.title: TOGO: OAU leaders urge Zaire talks before truce.
newsitem.headline: OAU leaders urge Zaire talks before truce.

text.p: Organisation of African Unity (OAU) leaders called on Thursday for immediate talks between Zaire's warring parties before a truce, effectively backing the rebel stance on negotiations to end the conflict.

At the same time, the leaders, who held a special summit in Togo, urged all concerned with the conflict and all OAU members to support fully the five-point peace plan of U.N. and OAU special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun and to help him implement it.
The delegation from Zaire's central authorities in Kinshasa expressed reservations about the talks-before-truce element of the OAU leaders' final declaration.

"The (leaders) called for immediate negotiations between the government of Zaire and the Democratic Alliance for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, leading to a ceasefire and complete cessation of hostilities, in order to pave the way for the implementation of the said plan," the declaration said.
It "urged all parties concerned as well as all member states to fully support the mission and mandate of the special representative (Sahnoun) in the implmentation of the plan."
It "condemned all types of foreign military intervention and the use of mercenaries in Zaire". The Kinshasa delegation also expressed reservations about that.
Over a dozen heads of state met over two days as members of the Central Organ of the OAU Mechanism for Conflict, Prevention, Management and Resolution -- the body's first heads of state summit.

The final declaration urged the OAU and the U.N. secretary generals to cooperate for implementation of the Sahnoun plan, which calls for a truce, talks, restoration of dialogue, respect of Zaire's sovereignty and that of other states in the volatile region and proper care for refugees and displaced Zaireans.

The declaration appealed for all parties to help accelerate the voluntary repatriation of refugees in east Zaire while ensuring their safety and dignity and to create conditions for distribution of humanitarian aid.

It called for the disarmament and demobilisation of former Rwandan Hutu hardliners and the trial by the International Tribunal of any suspected of involvement in the 1994 genocide of minority Tutsis in Rwanda.
The declaration underscored the need for an international conference on peace, security and stability in the volatile Great Lakes region under OAU and U.N. auspices.
